MTF.general_explanation: Review the individual option rationales; faculty must validate all medical statements and keys before publication.
MTF.stem: Regarding preauricular sinus, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: A preauricular sinus is a congenital anomaly.
options.explanation: It results from an embryologic developmental anomaly.

options.label: B
options.text: Its usual opening is near the anterior root of the helix.
options.explanation: The pit is typically immediately anterior to the ascending helix.

options.label: C
options.text: Most asymptomatic pits require urgent excision.
options.explanation: Asymptomatic pits may be observed.

options.label: D
options.text: Recurrent infection is an indication to consider excision.
options.explanation: Excision after inflammation settles may prevent recurrence.

options.label: E
options.text: Its tract routinely opens into the middle ear.
options.explanation: A typical preauricular sinus is superficial and does not communicate with the middle ear.

MTF.stem: Regarding auricular perichondritis, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: The pinna cartilage depends on the perichondrium for nutrition.
options.explanation: Perichondrium supplies avascular cartilage.

options.label: B
options.text: The lobule is typically spared in isolated perichondritis.
options.explanation: The lobule has no auricular cartilage.

options.label: C
options.text: Pseudomonas is an important cause after cartilage piercing.
options.explanation: High-ear piercing can introduce Pseudomonas.

options.label: D
options.text: A subperichondrial abscess can lead to cartilage necrosis.
options.explanation: Separation of perichondrium compromises cartilage viability.

options.label: E
options.text: Perichondritis usually causes isolated middle-ear effusion.
options.explanation: Its main pathology involves the pinna cartilage and perichondrium.

MTF.stem: Regarding auricular hematoma, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: A blunt injury can produce a subperichondrial hematoma.
options.explanation: Shearing trauma separates perichondrium from cartilage.

options.label: B
options.text: Failure to treat may result in cauliflower ear.
options.explanation: Organized hematoma and fibrosis deform the auricle.

options.label: C
options.text: A compressive dressing is commonly used after drainage.
options.explanation: Compression reduces reaccumulation.

options.label: D
options.text: Auricular hematoma typically involves the middle-ear cavity.
options.explanation: Auricular hematoma is a collection adjacent to auricular cartilage following trauma, not a middle-ear effusion.

options.label: E
options.text: Hematoma commonly follows contact sports.
options.explanation: Wrestling and boxing are classic settings.

options.label: A
options.text: Ear piercing may precede auricular keloid formation.
options.explanation: Trauma to skin can trigger pathological scar growth.

options.label: B
options.text: A keloid extends beyond the original wound boundaries.
options.explanation: Expansion beyond wound edges distinguishes it from a hypertrophic scar.

options.label: C
options.text: Recurrence after excision alone can occur.
options.explanation: Surgery alone has an appreciable recurrence risk.

options.label: D
options.text: A keloid is an infection of the auricular cartilage.
options.explanation: It is an abnormal fibrous scar.

options.label: E
options.text: Intralesional corticosteroid may be used in management.

MTF.general_explanation: Review the individual option rationales; faculty must validate all medical statements and keys before publication.
MTF.stem: Regarding external ear anatomy, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: The auricular lobule contains no cartilage.
options.explanation: The lobule is mainly connective and fatty tissue.

options.label: B
options.text: The external auditory canal has cartilaginous and bony segments.
options.explanation: Its lateral third is cartilaginous and medial two-thirds bony.

options.label: C
options.text: Hair follicles are found mainly in the bony medial canal.
options.explanation: Hair follicles and ceruminous glands are predominantly in the cartilaginous lateral canal.

options.label: D
options.text: The tympanic membrane separates the external and middle ear.
options.explanation: It forms the medial boundary of the external canal.

options.label: E
options.text: The bony and cartilaginous portions of the normal external auditory canal have the same skin thickness.
options.explanation: The skin over the bony canal is much thinner and more adherent to periosteum than skin over the cartilaginous canal.

MTF.stem: Regarding congenital and inflammatory pinna disease, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: Microtia is a congenital malformation of the pinna.
options.explanation: The external ear is incompletely developed.

options.label: B
options.text: Preauricular pits may be familial.
options.explanation: Preauricular sinus anomalies sometimes follow familial patterns.

options.label: C
options.text: Isolated pinna cellulitis always spares the lobule.
options.explanation: Cellulitis may involve the cartilaginous pinna and lobule.

options.label: D
options.text: Inflamed cartilage requires attention to possible abscess formation.
options.explanation: An abscess threatens the cartilage blood supply.

options.label: E
options.text: A traumatic auricular hematoma can be managed with analgesics alone when the swelling is painless.
options.explanation: A painless or mildly painful auricular hematoma still risks cartilage deformity; appropriate drainage and compression are generally required.

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Pinna manipulation may provoke pain.
options.explanation: Canal inflammation causes tenderness with movement.

options.label: C
options.text: A bulging tympanic membrane defines otitis externa.
options.explanation: Bulging TM is characteristic of acute otitis media.

options.label: D
options.text: Topical preparations are commonly first-line.
options.explanation: Topical treatment reaches uncomplicated canal infection.

options.label: E

options.explanation: Uncomplicated disease generally does not need systemic antibiotics.

MTF.stem: Regarding otitis externa risks, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: Frequent water exposure can predispose to otitis externa.
options.explanation: Moisture disrupts protective canal conditions.

options.label: B
options.text: Cotton-bud trauma may predispose to infection.
options.explanation: Skin abrasions compromise the barrier.

options.label: C
options.text: An acidic canal milieu helps inhibit pathogens.
options.explanation: Canal acidity is part of local defense.

options.label: D
options.text: Diabetes has no relevance to complicated external ear infections.
options.explanation: Diabetes increases concern for invasive necrotizing infection.

options.label: E
options.text: Aggressive instrumentation is routine prevention.
options.explanation: Instrumentation may injure the canal.

MTF.stem: Regarding otomycosis features, mark each statement True or False.

options.label: A
options.text: Pruritus is a common complaint.
options.explanation: Fungal canal infection commonly causes itching.

options.label: B
options.text: Aspergillus species may cause otomycosis.
options.explanation: Aspergillus is a recognized fungus in otomycosis.

options.label: C
options.text: Candida species can cause otomycosis.
options.explanation: Candida is another recognized cause.

options.label: D
options.text: A gray-white or black fungal debris may be seen.
options.explanation: Fungal material and spores may be visible on otoscopy.

options.label: E
options.text: In uncomplicated otomycosis, the fungal infection primarily involves the middle-ear mucosa.
options.explanation: Uncomplicated otomycosis is a superficial fungal infection involving the external auditory canal, not primarily the middle ear.

options.label: B
